title: A read and a write through DAX
claim: DAX answers cache hits from memory and sends misses, writes and strongly consistent reads on to the table.
alt: A sequence with three participants: an application with the DAX client, the DAX cluster and the DynamoDB table. A read that DAX has cached returns from DAX. A read that DAX has not cached goes on to the table, and DAX keeps the item. A write goes to the table first, then to DAX. A strongly consistent read goes through DAX to the table.

messages.label: Read
messages.say: The DAX client directs all of your application's DynamoDB API requests to the DAX cluster.

messages.label: Hit: from memory
messages.say: On a cache hit, DAX returns the item with microsecond latency.

messages.label: Miss: read table
messages.say: On a cache miss, DAX sends the request to DynamoDB and keeps the returned item in its item cache.

messages.label: Write first
messages.say: A write is first written to the DynamoDB table and then to DAX.

messages.label: Strong read: pass on
messages.say: DAX passes strongly consistent read requests to DynamoDB and does not cache the results.
